questions.text: Which utility class sets an element's text color to red in Tailwind CSS?
questions.explanation: The `text-{color}` utility sets the text color of an element. `text-red-500` applies a medium red from Tailwind's default color palette.

questions.text: How do you apply a background color of blue in Tailwind CSS?
questions.explanation: The `bg-{color}` utility applies a background color. `bg-blue-500` sets the background to a medium blue from the default palette.

questions.text: Which class makes an element use flexbox layout?
questions.explanation: `flex` sets `display: flex` on an element, enabling flexbox layout so child elements can be arranged using flex utilities.

questions.text: Which utility adds padding on all four sides of an element?
questions.explanation: The `p-{size}` utility applies equal padding to all sides of an element. For example, `p-4` applies 1rem of padding on all sides.

questions.text: How do you add a margin only to the top of an element in Tailwind?
questions.explanation: `mt-{size}` applies margin to the top only. The `t` stands for top, and the number maps to a spacing scale value.

questions.text: Which class makes text bold in Tailwind CSS?
questions.explanation: `font-bold` sets `font-weight: 700`, making text appear bold. It is part of Tailwind's font-weight utility group.

questions.text: Which Tailwind utility hides an element visually by setting display to none?
questions.explanation: `hidden` sets `display: none`, completely removing the element from the document flow and hiding it from view.

questions.text: What does the `rounded` class do in Tailwind CSS?
questions.explanation: `rounded` applies a small border-radius to all corners of an element, giving it slightly rounded edges. Larger variants like `rounded-lg` or `rounded-full` increase the radius.

answerOptions.text: Applies a default border-radius to all corners

questions.text: Which utility sets the width of an element to 100% of its parent?
questions.explanation: `w-full` sets `width: 100%`, making the element span the full width of its containing block.

questions.text: Which class centers flex children horizontally along the main axis?
questions.explanation: `justify-center` sets `justify-content: center`, centering flex (or grid) children along the main axis, which is horizontal by default.

questions.text: Which utility controls the font size in Tailwind?
questions.explanation: The `text-{size}` utilities like `text-sm`, `text-lg`, or `text-2xl` control font size. They map to predefined rem values in the default theme.

questions.text: What does `border` do on its own in Tailwind?
questions.explanation: `border` applies a 1px solid border using the current border color. It sets `border-width: 1px` without specifying color or style separately.

answerOptions.text: Adds a border only to the bottom

questions.text: How do you make an element take up the full viewport height in Tailwind?
questions.explanation: `h-screen` sets `height: 100vh`, making the element fill the full height of the browser viewport.

questions.text: Which class stacks flex children vertically?
questions.explanation: `flex-col` sets `flex-direction: column`, causing flex children to stack vertically instead of the default horizontal row.

questions.text: Which Tailwind class makes text italic?
questions.explanation: `italic` applies `font-style: italic` to the element's text. Its counterpart `not-italic` resets it to normal.

questions.text: Which utility applies horizontal padding (left and right) only?
questions.explanation: `px-{size}` applies padding to the left and right sides only. The `x` refers to the horizontal axis.

questions.text: What does `opacity-50` do in Tailwind?
questions.explanation: `opacity-50` sets the element's opacity to 50%, making it semi-transparent. The scale runs from `opacity-0` (invisible) to `opacity-100` (fully visible).

questions.text: What does the `sm:` prefix do in Tailwind CSS?
questions.explanation: `sm:` is a responsive breakpoint modifier that applies the utility only when the viewport is at least 640px wide (the default `sm` breakpoint).

answerOptions.text: Applies the utility only on small screens (below 640px)
Applies the utility on screens 640px and wider
Applies the utility on all screen sizes
Applies the utility only on mobile devices

questions.text: How do you apply a style only when an element is hovered in Tailwind?
questions.explanation: The `hover:` variant prefix applies a utility only when the user hovers over the element, using the CSS `:hover` pseudo-class under the hood.

questions.text: What is the purpose of the `group` class in Tailwind?
questions.explanation: Adding `group` to a parent element allows child elements to style themselves based on the parent's state using `group-hover:`, `group-focus:`, etc.

answerOptions.text: It groups multiple elements into a flex container
It enables children to react to the parent's hover or focus state
It creates a CSS grid group
It applies shared styles to sibling elements

questions.text: Which utility adds a box shadow to an element in Tailwind?
questions.explanation: `shadow-md` applies a medium box shadow. Tailwind provides a shadow scale from `shadow-sm` to `shadow-2xl`, plus `shadow-none` to remove shadows.

questions.text: What does `truncate` do in Tailwind CSS?
questions.explanation: `truncate` combines `overflow: hidden`, `text-overflow: ellipsis`, and `white-space: nowrap` to clip overflowing text and show an ellipsis.

answerOptions.text: Removes characters beyond a set limit
Clips overflowing text and adds an ellipsis
Wraps text onto the next line

questions.text: Which utility positions an element absolutely relative to its nearest positioned ancestor?
questions.explanation: `absolute` sets `position: absolute`, removing the element from normal flow and positioning it relative to the nearest ancestor with a non-static position.

questions.text: What is the default behavior of Tailwind's `dark:` variant?
questions.explanation: By default, the `dark:` variant activates when the user's operating system is set to dark mode, using the `prefers-color-scheme: dark` media query.

answerOptions.text: It activates when a `.dark` class is on the HTML element
It activates based on the OS/browser dark mode preference
It activates when a `data-theme='dark'` attribute is present
It must be manually triggered via JavaScript

questions.text: How do you use an arbitrary value for padding in Tailwind CSS?
questions.explanation: Tailwind's arbitrary value syntax uses square brackets to pass any CSS value directly, like `p-[13px]`, bypassing the default spacing scale.

questions.text: What does `space-x-4` do in Tailwind?
questions.explanation: `space-x-4` adds horizontal margin between sibling elements using a CSS sibling selector. It applies `margin-left` to all children except the first.

answerOptions.text: Adds 4px padding to the left of each child
Adds horizontal space between sibling elements using margin
Sets the gap between grid columns

questions.text: Which utility controls the number of columns in a CSS grid layout?
questions.explanation: `grid-cols-{n}` sets `grid-template-columns: repeat(n, minmax(0, 1fr))`, creating a grid with a fixed number of equal-width columns.

questions.text: What does the `ring` utility apply in Tailwind CSS?
questions.explanation: `ring` applies a box-shadow-based outline ring around an element, commonly used for focus indicators. It defaults to a 3px ring using the `ring-color`.

answerOptions.text: A box-shadow ring around the element

questions.text: How do you apply a transition to all properties in Tailwind?
questions.explanation: `transition-all` sets `transition-property: all`, enabling CSS transitions on every animatable property when combined with a `duration-` and `ease-` utility.

questions.text: What does `overflow-hidden` do in Tailwind?
questions.explanation: `overflow-hidden` sets `overflow: hidden`, clipping any content that extends beyond the element's bounds and preventing scroll.

answerOptions.text: Clips content that overflows the element's bounds
Adds a scrollbar when content overflows
Collapses the element when it overflows

questions.text: Which class applies a CSS `z-index` of 10 in Tailwind?
questions.explanation: `z-10` sets `z-index: 10`. Tailwind includes z-index utilities from `z-0` to `z-50` in increments defined by the theme.

questions.text: What does `gap-4` do when applied to a flex or grid container?
questions.explanation: `gap-4` sets the gap between flex or grid items to 1rem (the 4-step on the spacing scale). It applies to both row and column gaps uniformly.

answerOptions.text: Adds 4px margin around each child element
Sets 1rem spacing between flex or grid children

questions.text: Which utility makes an image cover its container without distortion?
questions.explanation: `object-cover` sets `object-fit: cover`, scaling the image to fill its container while preserving its aspect ratio, cropping as needed.

questions.text: What does the `peer` class enable in Tailwind CSS?
questions.explanation: Adding `peer` to an input or sibling element lets subsequent siblings style themselves based on its state using variants like `peer-focus:` or `peer-checked:`.

answerOptions.text: It creates a CSS peer-to-peer connection between elements
It allows sibling elements to react to the marked element's state
It shares styles between two components
It links two elements with the same class name

questions.text: Which utility applies styles only when an element has focus in Tailwind?
questions.explanation: `focus:` is a variant that applies utilities only when the element is focused via keyboard or click, using the CSS `:focus` pseudo-class.

questions.text: In Tailwind v4, how is the configuration file format different from v3?
questions.explanation: Tailwind v4 moves configuration into a CSS file using `@theme` directives instead of a `tailwind.config.js` file, making CSS the single source of truth for design tokens.

answerOptions.text: v4 uses a JSON file instead of JavaScript
v4 replaces the JS config file with CSS-based `@theme` configuration
v4 requires both a JS config and a CSS config file

questions.text: What does the `@layer` directive do in a Tailwind CSS file?
questions.explanation: `@layer` lets you inject styles into Tailwind's `base`, `components`, or `utilities` layers, controlling cascade order and allowing styles to be purged correctly.

answerOptions.text: It imports an external CSS file into the project
It injects styles into a specific Tailwind cascade layer
It creates a new CSS custom property layer
It marks styles as high-priority overrides

questions.text: What is the purpose of the `@apply` directive in Tailwind?
questions.explanation: `@apply` lets you compose Tailwind utility classes inside a CSS rule, useful for extracting repeated utility combinations into a reusable class while keeping the utility-first workflow.

answerOptions.text: It composes Tailwind utilities inside a CSS class definition
It applies a global theme override

questions.text: How do you reference a theme value inside custom CSS using Tailwind v3?
questions.explanation: The `theme()` function lets you reference values from your Tailwind configuration inside CSS, such as `color: theme('colors.blue.500')`, keeping CSS in sync with your design tokens.

questions.text: What is the role of the `content` array in `tailwind.config.js`?
questions.explanation: The `content` array tells Tailwind which files to scan for class names. Only classes found in these files are included in the production CSS, enabling effective purging of unused styles.

answerOptions.text: It lists CSS files to import into the build
It specifies files Tailwind scans to detect used class names for purging
It defines the content of the base layer
It sets which components are available in the project

questions.text: How do you add a custom plugin to Tailwind CSS?
questions.explanation: Custom plugins are added in the `plugins` array of `tailwind.config.js` using the `plugin()` helper from `tailwindcss/plugin`, which receives a set of helper functions to register utilities, components, or base styles.

answerOptions.text: By importing it in the CSS file with `@import`
By adding it to the `plugins` array in `tailwind.config.js`
By placing it in a `tailwind-plugins/` folder

questions.text: What does `tailwind-merge` solve that plain Tailwind CSS does not?
questions.explanation: `tailwind-merge` resolves class conflicts when merging Tailwind class strings — for example, ensuring `p-4` correctly overrides `p-2` instead of both being applied, which standard string concatenation cannot handle.

answerOptions.text: It adds missing utilities not included in Tailwind's core
It resolves conflicting Tailwind class names when merging class strings
It purges unused classes at build time

questions.text: Which Tailwind variant applies styles only when the user's preference is reduced motion?
questions.explanation: `motion-reduce:` applies utilities only when the user has enabled the 'reduce motion' accessibility setting, using the `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` media query.

questions.text: How do you enable the `class` strategy for dark mode in Tailwind v3?
questions.explanation: Setting `darkMode: 'class'` in `tailwind.config.js` makes the `dark:` variant activate when a `.dark` class is present on the `<html>` element, enabling manual JavaScript-controlled dark mode toggling.

answerOptions.text: Add `@dark class` in the CSS file

questions.text: What does `@screen md` do inside a Tailwind CSS file?
questions.explanation: `@screen md` is a Tailwind directive that expands to the `md` breakpoint's min-width media query, letting you write responsive styles in plain CSS using your configured breakpoints.

answerOptions.text: It applies styles only on medium-sized screens below 768px
It expands to the `md` breakpoint's min-width media query
It sets the container max-width to the md breakpoint

questions.text: What is the purpose of the `prettier-plugin-tailwindcss` package?
questions.explanation: This Prettier plugin automatically sorts Tailwind class names in your HTML and JSX according to Tailwind's recommended class order, keeping class lists consistent across a codebase.

answerOptions.text: It automatically sorts Tailwind class names in the recommended order
It validates that only valid Tailwind classes are used
It removes duplicate Tailwind classes on save

questions.text: How do you extend Tailwind's color palette without replacing the defaults?
questions.explanation: Placing custom colors inside `theme.extend.colors` merges them with the default palette. Using `theme.colors` directly replaces all defaults, removing built-in colors like `gray`, `blue`, etc.

questions.text: What does the `supports-` variant do in Tailwind CSS?
questions.explanation: `supports-[property:value]:` applies a utility only when the browser supports a given CSS feature, using the `@supports` rule under the hood for progressive enhancement.

answerOptions.text: It checks whether a Tailwind plugin is installed
It applies styles only when the browser supports a specific CSS feature

questions.text: In Tailwind v4, what replaces the `tailwind.config.js` `prefix` option?
questions.explanation: In Tailwind v4, the utility prefix is configured directly in CSS using `@layer utilities` with a namespace or via the `@import` with prefix option, as the JS config file is no longer the primary configuration mechanism.

answerOptions.text: The `--prefix` CLI flag at build time only
CSS-based configuration via the `@import` with prefix option

questions.text: Which variant applies styles to an element only when it is the first child of its parent?
questions.explanation: `first:` applies utilities using the `:first-child` CSS pseudo-class, targeting only the first sibling element within a parent — useful for removing top borders or margins on the leading item.

questions.text: What is a container query in the context of Tailwind CSS?
questions.explanation: Container queries (available via the official `@tailwindcss/container-queries` plugin or built into v4) let you apply styles based on the size of a parent container rather than the viewport, enabling truly component-level responsiveness.

answerOptions.text: A query that limits the max-width of the `.container` class
Styles that apply based on the width of a parent container element
A CSS query targeting only block-level container elements
A Tailwind utility for querying the DOM at runtime

questions.text: What does `subgrid` enable when used with Tailwind's grid utilities?
questions.explanation: `grid-cols-subgrid` (available in Tailwind v3.4+) sets `grid-template-columns: subgrid`, allowing a nested grid to inherit its column tracks from the parent grid for precise alignment across levels.

answerOptions.text: It creates a secondary grid inside a flex container
It allows a nested grid to inherit column tracks from its parent grid
It subdivides existing grid cells into smaller units
